title: Free Transcription and Caption Tools Directory
subtitle: Free no-account transcription and caption tools — cost, platform, setup steps, and official links. Includes free tiers and local options.
credits: Published by Asdale Dynamics, LLC (Indiana, formed Oct 2026). Beginner-friendly AI education, books, and practical tools.

tools.name: Windows Live Captions
tools.costDetail: Built into Windows 11 at no extra cost; runs locally on your PC
tools.setup: Press Windows+Ctrl+L to turn Live Captions on. Download the language pack when prompted, then pick your caption style and microphone source in Settings > Accessibility > Captions. Works for any audio playing on your PC, including microphone input.

tools.name: macOS Live Captions
tools.costDetail: Built into macOS at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open System Settings > Accessibility > Live Captions (beta) and turn it on. Captions appear in a floating window for any audio playing on your Mac.

tools.name: iOS Live Captions
tools.costDetail: Built into iOS 16 and later at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open Settings > Accessibility > Live Captions (beta) and turn it on. Type-to-speak responses are also supported during FaceTime and phone calls.

tools.name: Chrome Live Caption
tools.costDetail: Built into the Chrome browser at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open Chrome Settings > Accessibility and turn on Live Caption. Captions appear automatically for videos and audio playing in Chrome tabs.

tools.name: Live Transcribe & Sound Notifications
tools.costDetail: Free app from Google
tools.setup: Install Live Transcribe from the Play Store, then enable it in Settings > Accessibility > Live Transcribe. It transcribes speech in real time and can alert you to sounds like doorbells or alarms.

tools.name: Android Select to Speak
tools.costDetail: Built into Android at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open Settings > Accessibility > Select to Speak and turn it on. Tap the Play button or tap items on screen to hear them read aloud.

tools.name: Windows Dictation
tools.costDetail: Built into Windows at no extra cost
tools.setup: Press Windows+H in any text field to start dictation. Say punctuation like 'period' or 'comma' as you speak. Enable online speech recognition in Settings > Privacy & security > Speech.

tools.name: Windows Voice Access
tools.costDetail: Built into Windows 11 at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open Settings > Accessibility > Speech > Voice Access and turn it on. Download the language pack when prompted, then say 'Voice Access wake up' to begin controlling your PC and dictating by voice.

tools.name: macOS Dictation
tools.costDetail: Built into macOS at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open System Settings > Keyboard > Dictation and turn it on. Press the Fn key (or the Dictation key) twice to start speaking wherever you can type.

tools.name: macOS Voice Control
tools.costDetail: Built into macOS at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open System Settings > Accessibility > Voice Control and turn it on. Number overlays and a grid let you click, scroll, and navigate entirely by voice.

tools.name: iOS Dictation
tools.costDetail: Built into iOS at no extra cost
tools.setup: Open Settings > General > Keyboard and turn on Enable Dictation. Tap the microphone icon on the keyboard to dictate text in any app.

tools.name: Gboard Voice Typing
tools.costDetail: Free keyboard app from Google
tools.setup: Install Gboard from the Play Store (Android) or App Store (iOS), set it as your keyboard, then tap the microphone icon on the keyboard to dictate text.

tools.name: OpenAI Whisper (local)
tools.costDetail: Free and open source; runs locally on your own computer via Python/pip
tools.setup: Install Python from python.org, then run `pip install faster-whisper`. Transcribe a file with `python -m faster_whisper transcribe audio.mp3 --model base --output_format txt`. No audio leaves your computer.

tools.name: Whisper.cpp
tools.costDetail: Free and open source C++ port of Whisper; fast on CPU, no Python needed
tools.setup: Download a prebuilt binary from the GitHub releases page (or install with `brew install whisper.cpp` on Mac). Run `whisper-cli -m models/ggml-base.en.bin -f meeting.wav -of output` to get a local transcript.

tools.name: Vosk
tools.costDetail: Free and open source lightweight speech recognition; small offline models
tools.setup: Download a model from alphacephei.com/vosk/models, then use the Vosk API or command-line tool to transcribe audio offline. Models are around 50 MB, so it runs on low-end hardware.

tools.name: oTranscribe
tools.costDetail: Free and open source web-based transcription player; no account required
tools.setup: Open otranscribe.com in any browser. Upload your audio or video file, then play it in the built-in player and type the transcript in the same window. Your audio stays in your browser — nothing is uploaded.

tools.name: Google Docs Voice Typing
tools.costDetail: Free; requires a free Google account
tools.setup: Open docs.google.com in Chrome or Edge, create a new document, then click Tools > Voice typing. Click the microphone icon and speak — text appears in real time. Sign in with a free Google account.

tools.name: YouTube Auto-Captions
tools.costDetail: Free; requires a free Google/YouTube account
tools.setup: Go to studio.youtube.com and sign in. Upload your video as Unlisted, wait for YouTube to generate auto-captions, then go to Subtitles > your video > English (Automatic) and download the captions as .vtt, .srt, or .txt.

tools.name: Subtitle Edit
tools.costDetail: Free and open source subtitle/caption editor for Windows
tools.setup: Download and install Subtitle Edit from subtitleedit.org. Open an .srt or .vtt caption file, fix timing and text, then save. You can also create captions from scratch and sync them to audio.

tools.name: Aegisub
tools.costDetail: Free and open source subtitle/caption editor for Windows, macOS, and Linux
tools.setup: Download Aegisub from aegisub.org and install it for your operating system. Open a subtitle file, edit the text and timing with the built-in audio player and waveform, then save as .ass, .srt, or .vtt.
